families.source: UKHSA administration guidance for rabies vaccine and human rabies immunoglobulin
families.topic: post-exposure rabies vaccine scheduling, HRIG dosing, wound infiltration and administration-site separation
families.page_title: Administration of rabies vaccine and immunoglobulin
evidence_points: Rabies post-exposure vaccine is administered intramuscularly in the deltoid muscle.
The UK schedule for unimmunised individuals uses vaccine on days 0, 3, 7 and 21.
Day 0 is the day the first vaccine is given rather than necessarily the exposure date.
If a dose is missed, it should be given as soon as possible and later intervals readjusted.
The final dose in the standard four-dose schedule should not be given before day 21.
HRIG is added according to the exposure risk assessment to provide short-term passive protection.
HRIG should be infiltrated into and around the wound where possible.
Rabies vaccine and HRIG must not be administered at the same anatomical site.
HRIG is not normally used after 7 days from starting vaccine or for a person already partially immunised.
The calculated HRIG dose depends on patient weight and product potency; the entire vial must not be given automatically.

families.source: UKHSA interim recommendations for human rabies immunoglobulin use
families.topic: HRIG prioritisation, wound infiltration, timing limits and high-risk rabies exposure management
families.page_title: Interim recommendations for human rabies immunoglobulin (HRIG) use
evidence_points: UKHSA issued interim recommendations to prioritise HRIG for people at greatest rabies risk.
HRIG provides immediate passive antibody at the wound site until vaccine-induced immunity develops.
Existing guidance uses HRIG for specified category 3 exposures and severely immunosuppressed people.
The maximum HRIG dose is based on 20 international units per kilogram body weight.
HRIG should be infiltrated into and around the cleansed wound wherever possible.
Intramuscular administration away from the wound provides limited benefit compared with wound infiltration.
HRIG is not indicated more than 7 days after the first vaccine dose.
HRIG is not indicated more than one day after the second vaccine dose.
HRIG can be diluted with saline when extra volume is needed to infiltrate multiple severe wounds.
Eligibility still depends on the full rabies exposure risk assessment, immune status and vaccine history.

families.source: UKHSA rabies post-exposure treatment management guidelines
families.topic: rabies exposure risk assessment, vaccine, HRIG, country risk and prompt post-exposure treatment
evidence_points: The guidance provides a practical risk-assessment framework for potential rabies exposures.
It is intended for UKHSA duty doctors, health protection teams and other involved health professionals.
Rabies is a viral encephalitis that is almost invariably fatal after symptoms develop.
Prompt post-exposure treatment is the principal method of preventing disease after a significant exposure.
Treatment may use rabies vaccine alone or vaccine with HRIG depending on assessed risk.
The latest country-risk list should be used rather than relying on an older list embedded in guidance.
Exposure assessment includes animal species, country, circumstances and the type of contact.
Previous vaccination and immune status change the recommended treatment schedule.
Interim HRIG recommendations supersede the HRIG sections of the wider management document.
A bite or animal contact alone does not define treatment; the composite risk assessment determines action.

families.source: UKHSA rabies risk assessment and treatment summary
families.topic: composite rabies risk categories and vaccine or HRIG treatment schedules
families.page_title: Rabies: summary of risk assessment and treatment (text version)
evidence_points: The summary combines country, animal and exposure factors into a composite rabies risk.
Composite risk is grouped into green, amber or red treatment categories.
Green risk does not require post-exposure treatment.
Amber risk generally requires vaccine for non-immunised people.
Red risk generally requires vaccine and HRIG for non-immunised people, subject to current interim HRIG rules.
Fully immunised people generally receive a shorter vaccine schedule after amber or red exposures.
Immunosuppressed people may require HRIG and a five-dose vaccine schedule for amber or red risk.
Specific animal and bat advice can modify the interpretation of the summary tables.
HRIG timing restrictions remain relevant once vaccination has begun.
The summary table does not replace the detailed exposure history, current country risk and clinical assessment.

families.source: UKHSA rabies post-exposure risk assessment form and vaccine calendar
families.topic: structured rabies exposure documentation, HRIG calculation, vaccine scheduling and treatment records
families.page_title: Rabies post exposure risk assessment form and calendar
evidence_points: The publication provides a structured form for documenting potential rabies exposure.
It supports recording the country, animal, exposure type and prior vaccination status.
It includes a calendar for scheduling rabies post-exposure vaccine doses.
It supports calculation and recording of the required HRIG volume when indicated.
Current HRIG batch potency must be used in the dose-volume calculation.
Completed risk-assessment information is used by the Rabies and Immunoglobulin Service.
Treatment records should include vaccine dates and any HRIG administration.
Interim HRIG recommendations must be applied alongside the form.
Concern about a potentially falsified vaccine requires specialist UKHSA advice rather than assumptions about protection.
The form supports but does not replace professional assessment of the exposure and treatment response.
